Andriyevo-Ivanivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Andriyevo-Ivanivka, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably existing by the late 19th century, this cemetery was likely ruined during or after WWII, though postwar burials continued until 1981. Little documentation survives about the community itself; a synagogue existed by 1873, and population reached 546 (38%) by 1897, with a Jewish savings bank operating from 1912. Population fell to 330 by 1939. German-Romanian occupation from August 5, 1941 eventually killed 60 Jews; in March 1942, 165 Jews from Odesa were also killed in the town. In total, 236 Jews from Andriyevo-Ivanivka were murdered during WWII, though epigraphic evidence shows Jewish presence continuing into the 1980s.
